residual_risks: The new controlled-value path delegates stale-result suppression to useFieldValidation.commit's generation check. A later non-undefined controlled value calls validation.change and supersedes an older pending commit. A controlled-to-uncontrolled transition is skipped by the new callback, so it does not itself invalidate an in-flight commit; React generally discourages changing control mode, and the DOM may retain its prior value in that transition.

The existing validation hook has no explicit unmount cleanup to invalidate pending async commits. This is a pre-existing lifecycle behavior also reachable through user-triggered validation; the new path can now start such work from a programmatic controlled change.
testing_gaps: No test covers an async validator for controlled value A resolving after a programmatic change to B; the implementation appears to suppress this through the existing commit generation check, but a regression test would pin that behavior.
No test covers a controlled-value async validation resolving after Field.Control unmounts while Field.Root remains mounted.
